podcast.title: 21st Birthday Party Destruction (August 23, 1967)
podcast.body: Keith Moon, the "king of hotel room demolition," celebrated his 21st birthday on August 23, 1967, at the Holiday Inn in Flint, Michigan, resulting in a "crazy party" that left the hotel a "disaster." Legend has it that a Lincoln Continental, driven by Keith Moon, ended up in the swimming pool, initiating the "rock and roll cliche." The hotel damage amounted to $24,000 in 1967, which is approximately $200,000 today. "Legend is that a Lincoln Continental driven by Keith ended up in the swimming pool."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Godfather to Zach Starkey
podcast.body: Keith Moon of The Who was the godfather of Zach Starkey and gave him his first drum kit. "He got his first kit from Keith Moon of the Who, who was also his godfather."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Banned from Holiday Inn (Post-1967)
xref.body: The Who is permanently banned from staying at any Holiday Inn chain hotels following the extensive damage caused by Keith Moon's 21st birthday party at the Flint, Michigan Holiday Inn on August 23, 1967. "The who is still banned from staying at any holiday in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Accidental Death of Chauffeur (January 4, 1970)
xref.body: On January 4, 1970, outside the Red Lion Pub near London, Keith Moon's car was pelted with rocks and bottles by a crowd of skinheads. His chauffeur, Neil Bowen, stepped out to try and calm the situation. In a panic, Moon, who did not have a driver's license, jumped behind the wheel and hit the accelerator, trapping and dragging Bowen beneath the car, leading to his death in hospital. "On January 4, 1970, Keith ran into an angry crowd outside the Red Lion Pub near London, a group of skinheads went after Moon and his Bentley pelting it with rocks and bottles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Early Introduction to Sex, Drugs, and Rock and Roll (Childhood)
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis, born in Grand Rapids, Michigan, moved to California at age 12 to live with his father, Blackie Dammit, who was a bit-part actor and drug dealer in Hollywood. Kiedis was exposed to drugs from a young age; at four, his father blew pot smoke in his face. His father's lifestyle involved frequent clubbing on Sunset Strip and bringing various women home. By age 12, Kiedis was accompanying his father to clubs, using quaaludes given by his father, and even propositioning one of his father's girlfriends, Kimberly, with his father's consent, leading to a sexual encounter while his father watched TV. Keith Moon was also an adult friend and role model to Kiedis during this period. "The Chilling Febrero's with Anthony Kedis, who was introduced to the world of sex, drugs and rock and roll fully by the time he was 12."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Brad Wilk's Background and Influences
xref.body: Brad Wilk, originally from Chicago, started out as a guitarist before becoming a fan of The Who's drummer, Keith Moon. He pursued jazz drumming lessons from serious pros, idolizing Elvin Jones, from whom he learned funky grooves. He also studied James Brown and George Clinton records, mastering the technique of inserting a microsecond delay into his timekeeping, crucial for a good groove. "He also studied James Brown and George Clinton records and learned how to insert a microsecond delay into his time keeping something that's essential to a good groove."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Charges and Outcome
xref.body: Keith Moon was charged with drunk driving and driving without a license following the incident. However, the tragedy was ultimately treated as an accident, minimizing the legal consequences beyond the immediate charges. "Moon was charged with drunk driving and driving without a license, but on the whole the tragedy was treated as an accident."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Controversial Public Display
xref.body: Keith Moon of The Who was known for engaging in various peculiar acts, including a particularly controversial incident where he walked through a Jewish neighborhood in London while dressed as a Nazi, causing widespread offense. "Keith Moon of the Who, he did all kinds of weird things like walking through a Jewish neighborhood in London while dressed as a Nazi."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Drummer Zach Starkey
xref.body: Zach Starkey, son of Ringo Starr, secured a gig with The Who and has been their on-call drummer for live performances ever since. His godfather, Keith Moon, was also The Who's drummer. "He got a gig with The Who, which seems fitting, given his family history. And since then, he's been on call with them whenever the Who plays live."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Drumming & Influences – Beatles and Keith Moon
xref.body: Growing up, Jeff Hyman (later Joey Ramone) was a big fan of The Beatles. He acquired a snare drum and high hats by trading supermarket stamps his mom collected, allowing him to play along with Beatles records. At 13, his grandmother gave him a full drum set, which he expanded to match the size of Keith Moon's kit, who was his drumming hero. "Jeff got his mom to trade her stamps for a snare drum and a set of high hats so he could play along with his Beatles records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Influences
xref.body: While growing up and playing in local bands, Neil Peart was deeply influenced by prominent drummers across different genres. He admired Keith Moon of The Who, Ginger Baker of Cream, John Bonham of Led Zeppelin, and Mitch Mitchell of The Jimi Hendrix Experience. Additionally, he was fascinated by big band drummers such as Gene Krupa and Buddy Rich. "He loved Keith Moon of the Who, ginger baker of cream, John Bonham of Zeppelin, and Mitch Mitchell of Jimmy Hendrix's groove."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Life and Exposure to Drugs and Sex (Childhood)
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis moved to California to live with his father, Blackie Dammit, a bit-part actor and Hollywood drug dealer, at the age of 12. He recounted in his memoir, "Scar Tissue," an incident at age four where his father blew pot smoke in his face on Sunset Strip. By the time he was 12, Kiedis was clubbing with his father, taking quaaludes provided by his father, and even proposed a sexual encounter with one of his father's girlfriends, Kimberly, which his father facilitated. Keith Moon was an adult friend and role model to Kiedis during his pre-teen years. "When I was about four, my dad and I were on one of our outings walking down sunset strip. When he suddenly stopped and gently blew some pot smoke in my face."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Godfather and First Drum Kit
xref.body: Zach Starkey, son of Ringo Starr and Maureen, received his first drum kit from his godfather, Keith Moon of The Who. "Just like dad, he plays drums. He got his first kit from Keith Moon of the Who, who was also his godfather."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Keith Moon's Friendship with Young Anthony Kiedis (Childhood)
xref.body: Keith Moon was an adult friend and role model to Anthony Kiedis during Kiedis's formative years, when Kiedis was not yet a teenager. This association exposed young Kiedis to a particular lifestyle, with Moon being described as an adult role model for someone so young. "One adult who became friends with Anthony was Keith Moon."
